items.a: MSAR is open to mathematics and statistics students at every year of study. Our home is the University of Rwanda's College of Science and Technology, and our fellowship sessions also bring together students at the Gikondo campus. Graduates stay connected through our alumni network.

items.q: Do I need experience with data tools before joining?
items.a: No. Our sessions start from the fundamentals. Many members first opened KoboToolbox, Power BI or Python in an MSAR session.

items.q: How do I become a member?
items.a: Fill in the short membership form on the Join page. A member of the team will follow up with details of the next session and how to get involved.

items.q: When and where do activities happen?
items.a: Most activities take place in the evenings at UR–CST in Kigali. Every upcoming session is published on the Events page with its date, time and room.

items.q: Does MSAR offer internships or job placements?
items.a: MSAR connects members with career insights, mentors and partner organisations. We are exploring further career initiatives, including possible internship opportunities in 2027 — but nothing is confirmed yet. Members will hear first through official channels.

items.q: How can an organisation partner with MSAR?
items.a: We welcome organisations that want to run trainings, share career insights, host guest talks or support student research. Reach us through the Contact page or at info@msar.rw.
